items.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998
items.q: Working with Cleo Laine — some kind of special feeling I had about playing with her

ctx.x: You’ve been able to — in addition to having your own band — played with quite a list of people, and I wonder if there’s been some folks that have stood out in your mind as being really memorable experiences. © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

Oh a lot. And for different reasons too. Working with Cleo Laine — some kind of special feeling I had about playing with her, and it meant a lot to me. Playing with Charlie Haden and Ed Blackwell was probably the most exciting rhythm section I’ve ever worked with in my life, and I played the Village Vanguard with them. I mean I will never forget Blackwell, ever. I think Ed Blackwell, of the instrumentalists, Ed Blackwell probably had a more profound influence on me, absolutely, not because we talked about…
Was that a fairly spontaneous gig too?
